topIssues.title: kona-node: serve superroot_atTimestamp pre-interop from kona-safedb
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of #23473.

## Scope

Add `superroot_atTimestamp` to kona-node for the pre-interop (single chain, trivial dependency set) case. op-proposer in super-root mode, the ZK and super-root op-challenger paths, and op-dispute-mon read it.

The reference is op-node's `op-node/node/superroot_api.go`: `RequiredL1` and `VerifiedRequiredL1` come from `l1_at_safe_head` on the safedb, and the response must obey the contract in `op-service/eth/superroot_at_timestamp.go` (every L1 block strictly below `CurrentL1` fully processed; consumers gate on `CurrentL1 > X`).

Lokahi had a draft of the same shim in the closed #22626.

## Done

- [ ] Handler exists and is registered in the `superroot` namespace.
- [ ] `RequiredL1` fields come from the safedb and match op-node for the same timestamp on a devstack network.
- [ ] Behavior after a derivation reset is consistent with the contract (see #23247 for the accepted reading).
- [ ] Unit tests cover a recorded timestamp, a timestamp above local-safe, and the disabled state.

topIssues.title: Archive node snapshots contain a gap in historical data
topIssues.author: JB273
topIssues.body:
Hi team,

We are using the snapshot from https://datadirs.optimism.io/ and it appears to be so that the provided snapshot here holds a gap for historical data.
We use the RPC mainly on The Graph indexing and we see the same missing data there (which is obvious), we have consulted with another indexer/RPC provider and they see the same issue.
It looks that the server from where the snapshot was created was in a pruning state (or was before)!

A couple of questions, can you confirm (and test);

1. If the snapshot should hold the complete historical data (from the bedrock block obviously)
2. Check if the data is available for the request attached from the snapshots provided by datadirs.optimism.io

We tested with this below curl request:
```
curl -sS "$RPC" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "jsonrpc":"2.0",
    "method":"eth_call",
    "params":[
      {
        "to":"0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006",
        "data":"0x18160ddd"
      },
      {
        "blockHash":"0x093a99185048338f9a43a0877d3d9d7b012aa2bc7007f632b3690758b778f49d"
      }
    ],
    "id":2
  }'
```
Response:
`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"state at block #127302882 is pruned"}}`

topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: integration tests for kona-node safedb
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of #23473.

## Scope

Prove the integration end to end against kona-node, not just in unit tests.

Acceptance suites:

- Remove `SkipOnKonaNode` from `op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_elsync` and run `safeheaddb_clsync` against kona-node. Closes #22265.
- Run `TestExecuteStep_CannonKona` against kona-node. Closes #22279.
- Add an op-node parity check: on a network with one op-node and one kona-node verifier, `checkSafeHeadConsistent` passes with kona-node as the checked node and op-node as the source of truth, and the reverse.

Proofs stack:

- An output-root fault dispute game is played to resolution by an op-challenger whose only rollup node is kona-node.
- op-proposer in super-root mode and op-dispute-mon run against kona-node only.

Soak:

- A kona-node on a devnet runs 24 hours with the flag on and a contiguity check (safedb-scan from infrastructure-services, or an in-tree equivalent) reports no gap. Record restarts during the soak and confirm the history survives them.

## Done

- [ ] Both safeheaddb suites pass against kona-node in CI.
- [ ] `TestExecuteStep_CannonKona` passes against kona-node in CI.
- [ ] Parity test exists and passes.
- [ ] Challenger, proposer and dispute-mon tests against kona-node only exist and pass.
- [ ] Soak result is posted on #23473.

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock,op-core,op-supernode,kona: formal models and differential tests for interop message expiry
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Adds formal models, symbolic checks and differential tests for interop message expiry and `SuperchainETHBridge` refunds (#23259). They give reviewers machine-checked evidence that the shipped design cannot pay ETH twice: a message is never both relayed on its destination and refunded on its source. These models found the pre-staged-withdrawal double spend in the earlier design, where L1 trusted the L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger as the sender. That finding is why exports now come from the `UndeliveredMessageExporter` predeploy. They check that the landed design closes the gap. Without them, the safety argument rests on prose and unit tests.

No effect on users: everything is test or verification code. The Solidity under `test/formal/` compiles into the forge test build, and its Foundry invariant and fuzz suites run in contracts-bedrock CI with inline budgets. The Lean, Quint, Dafny, Halmos, Kontrol, hevm and EVMLean harnesses are not wired into CI; each directory's README says how to run it. The three Go/Rust tests run the real window-rule implementations against shared vectors.

The files live in a new `test/formal/expiry/` tree rather than `test/invariants/` and `test/kontrol/` because one argument spans several tools. `test/formal/expiry/README.md` maps each property to the tools that check it, and lists what is proved and what is assumed. The one-line `test-validation` exclusion is needed because these files have no matching `src/` path, as for `test/invariants/`.

Related: #23259.

Reviews: each layer was audited by a fresh-context reviewer and by two independent model reviewers; the outcomes are in each README's review log. `go-code-reviewer` and `rust-code-reviewer` are pending for the differential tests. `interop-reviewer` and `/security-review` are not run because this diff changes no production code; they apply to #23259.

topPRs.title: ci: add an optional RWX shadow that leaves CircleCI unchanged
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
Adds RWX as an optional shadow of the CircleCI PR workloads, without changing anything CircleCI runs. It replaces the approach of #23151, which rerouted about 66 CircleCI jobs through new evidence-collecting wrappers and edited justfiles and product code to feed them; that made CircleCI itself part of the experiment and hard to approve. Here CircleCI stays the only required CI, and RWX can be turned off or deleted without touching it.

**CircleCI is unchanged.** `git diff origin/develop -- .circleci justfile op-acceptance-tests rust/justfile packages op-deployer` is empty. Outside `.rwx/` and `ops/ci/`, the PR adds two CODEOWNERS lines (`/.rwx/` and `/ops/ci/` → cloud-security, as in #23151), the operator guide `docs/ai/rwx-shadow-ci.md`, and its index line in `AGENTS.md`.

**When RWX runs.** GitHub pushes to `develop`, and pushes to opt-in branches named `rwx/*`; plus RWX's `develop`-only cache-rebuild runs and manual `rwx run`. Contributor PRs never start a run or get an RWX status check (in #23151, `rust-e2e.yml` and `selector-upload.yml` fired on every branch push). None of the RWX checks is required.

**Cost.** Each `develop` push starts three RWX runs: `pr-gates.yml` (every shadowed PR workload, then the gate mirrors), `rust-e2e.yml` and `selector-upload.yml`. RWX may also start `develop`-only cache-rebuild runs. Teddy holds the cost figures privately; they are not published here. Pilot observation, not a measurement of this branch: on #23151's head (2216cd4069) the three runs took about 39, 19 and 2.5 minutes wall clock.

**Turning it off.** Set the `if:` of the three `on.github.push` triggers (`pr-gates.yml`, `rust-e2e.yml`, `selector-upload.yml`) to `false` and merge; or, immediately, a GitHub org owner suspends the RWX GitHub App or removes this repository from it. Deleting `.rwx/`, `ops/ci/`, the guide and the two CODEOWNERS lines removes it completely.

**Product-code hooks.** None remain. RWX now calls the unchanged recipes and scripts that CircleCI calls, or does the work in its own wrapper:

| #23151 hook | RWX here |
| --- | --- |
| `OP_DEPLOYER_TEST_BINARY` in `cli_runner_test.go` | The CLI test's `TestMain` builds op-deployer at verdict time, as on CircleCI: a cold build (about 35 s locally) on the four verdict workers that run the CLI groups, off the critical path |
| Runtime `CARGO_BIN_EXE_lokahi` lookup in `rust/lokahi/tests/cli.rs` | The unit-test worker extracts the nextest archive at the producer's target path, so the compile-time path resolves |
| Coverage replay in `go-ffi/trie*.go` | RWX runs coverage unseeded, like CircleCI |
| `vm.skip` reasons and the `DisputeGameFactory` fork fix in Solidity tests | Not needed: RWX runs the same fork configuration as CircleCI |
| Root `justfile`: Go runner and `_nut-prefork-state-for` reroutes | RWX runs its own Go runner over `just list-test-packages`, and the unchanged `just _check-nut-prefork-states` |
| `op-acceptance-tests/justfile` sharding and reports | The unchanged recipe; RWX answers its `circleci tests split` call with RWX's own shard plan |
| `rust/justfile` `print_commands` | The unchanged `hack` / `hack-tests-default` recipes, as CircleCI calls them |
| `nut-provenance-verify` reports, `test-interop-deposits-diff.sh` and `make-summary-deployment.sh` capture | The commands' exit status and logs |
| `ops/check-changed`, `.gitignore`, `.dockerignore` | Not needed: RWX does not call `check-changed`, its routing ignores `.ci/`, and no Docker build copies `.ci/` |
| `fetch-witness-tar.sh` retry | Owned by #23772; RWX inherits it when that lands |
| `generate-flaky-tests-report.sh` anonymous API access | The only one RWX cannot avoid, so this PR drops the flaky-report shadow instead. Restoring it needs that script change (acceptance-test owners) or a CircleCI API token in an RWX vault |

**What changed relative to #23151.** The first commit imports `.rwx/` and `ops/ci/` verbatim from 2216cd4069, so the later commits show every change.
- RWX selects workloads by running CircleCI's own routing data and policy (`.circleci/routing.yml`, `collect-params.sh`, `compute-workflow-conditions.sh`) read-only, instead of a forked copy. A change under `.rwx/` or `ops/ci/` selects every workload.
- Removed what only CircleCI used: the forked routing scripts and their decision-tree tests, the 19 parity comparers that read CircleCI wrapper evidence, CircleCI adapter tests, and orphaned contract scripts. Kept `compare-ci.py`, which compares RWX results with CircleCI's normal JUnit/Go JSON/test-metadata output, and `circle-alignment.py`, which fails when a CircleCI gate's `requires:` stops matching `pr-gates.json` (it passes against `develop`).
- Dropped the flaky-report shadow: it needs either the #23151 edit to `generate-flaky-tests-report.sh` (anonymous API access) or a CircleCI API token in an RWX vault.
- Removed every reference to `codex/rwx-ci-pilot`, including the pinned L2 fork snapshot; RWX forks OP Mainnet at `latest`, like CircleCI's PR job.
- Fixed verdicts that reported false failures: an all-skipped contract selection (now counted as executed, like `check-junit-tests-ran.sh`); passing `compile_fail` doctests and `#[should_panic]` tests in the Rust and SP1 reports; Go 1.24+ `build-output`/`build-fail` events in `ci-test-results.py`; Semgrep findings, which `--json` hid from the log, are printed again.
- Every `ops/ci` unit test runs in RWX when `ops/ci/` or `.rwx/` changes: such a change selects every workload, each workload's `helper-tests` task runs its tests, and the new `ci-unit-tests` task runs the shared ones. `test_ci_layout.py` fails when no task runs a test file.

**Trade-off.** CircleCI no longer emits the byte-level parity evidence that #23151's wrappers produced, so RWX results are compared with CircleCI's normal artifacts.

**Before `rwx/*` branches work end to end**, an RWX admin needs to grant `refs/heads/rwx/*` on the test-only `optimism-go-tests-rpc-shadow` vault. Its repository grants are `develop` and `codex/rwx-ci-pilot` today; the pilot grant can go once #23151 closes. The cache vault `optimism-op-reth-shadow` keeps its `develop`-only write grant.

**Validation.** `rwx lint --dir .rwx` reports no errors (19 warnings: `mise/install` 1.1.1 exists; this PR keeps the 1.1.0 that #23151 ran with). Locally, every `ops/ci` unit test passes (396 + 44; 41 live-toolchain fixtures skip on macOS and run inside their RWX tasks), `circle-alignment.py` passes against `develop`'s CircleCI config, and ShellCheck and shfmt are clean. No hosted RWX run has been made from this branch yet.

**Review.** A CI-config review and a code review both found that CircleCI's routing omits the flags it does not enable, which turned the RWX gates red on opt-in `rwx/*` pushes without contract or Rust changes; 3e784c8acb fixes it and the routing test now fails without the fix. Accepted without a code change, please confirm:
- `required-rust-e2e` has no alignment check: its job list in `ops/ci/runtime/rust-e2e.py` matches CircleCI today and must be kept in step by hand (documented).
- The routing adapter inherits CircleCI's fixed `/tmp/pipeline-parameters.json`. RWX tasks are isolated; only two concurrent local runs of `test_rwx_metadata.py` would collide.
- The import commit still has #23151's unconditional push triggers, so this PR must be squash-merged (the repository default) and that commit never pushed as a branch head.
- The runtime scripts keep their now-unused `--provider circleci` modes, to keep this diff close to #23151; removing them is a separate cleanup.

topPRs.title: kona-node,kona-engine!: execute engine commands through one owner
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
An unsafe backlog or execution RPC failure can trap reset control, and derivation currently has to infer success from engine callbacks. Give execution mutations and resets one owner with bounded admission, epoch checks, acknowledged outcomes and state publication before replies. This removes the task heap, forwarding operation clients and callback state machine while keeping the independent kona-node connected to an external execution client.

Derived rejection now uses the L1 inclusion timestamp, distinguishes INVALID from temporary statuses, and performs the deposits-only replacement only where required. Pending span progress stays separate from completed safe/finalized progress; finality records carry the actual accepted block hash and inclusion source. Sequencer retries retain the retrieved payload, and full engine admission leaves networking responsive.

Stacked on #23488. The tracked [implementation plan](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/kona-refactor-05-engine-owner/docs/ai/kona-node-pr-plan.md) records scope and the remaining stack. Read-only RPC and sequencer-admin forwarding remain for their planned follow-ups; bootstrap policy and the canonical reset walk are preserved. The force-inclusion verifier receives one real startup block, then derives through the outage without L2 peers or further unsafe injection; idle-start bootstrap remains PR10.

Closes #22681. Its forced-inclusion regression is preserved by #23494 without a verifier startup payload primer; #23495 validates the recovered safe/finalized chain with engine-owned finality.

BREAKING CHANGE: replaces public Engine/task/error-severity wrappers and operation forwarding clients with ordinary kona-engine operations and kona-node-service EngineHandle. Downstream composition constructs EngineActor together with its handle; derived imports use ImportMode, EngineState includes phase/epoch/pending-safe, and producers carry captured context instead of sending raw operation messages.

Local validation: 321 offline tests, 115 focused tests, full workspace Rust lint, full repository Go lint, and a fresh default node build pass. The real short-window force-inclusion regression passes with a Kona sequencer and isolated Kona verifier. Four existing reorg subcases across both presets and both Kona restart tests also pass. Independent Rust/protocol, Go and deletion/API reviews completed; all actionable findings were fixed.

topPRs.title: kona-node!: start conductor-managed sequencers stopped
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Conductor-managed Kona sequencers can become active on process startup without coordinated activation when `--sequencer.stopped` is omitted. They now always start stopped and wait for an explicit start, including when constructed directly through Rust.

Tenth PR in the stack, based on #23627. Preserves the remaining startup protection from #23578; #23581 and #23223 already supply its leadership checks and disaster-recovery behavior. Review against the immediate parent.

BREAKING CHANGE: Operators configuring `--conductor.rpc` must activate through conductor coordination, or explicitly call `admin_overrideLeader` followed by `admin_startSequencer` during disaster recovery. Leaving `--sequencer.stopped` unset no longer starts a conductor-managed sequencer automatically.

Validation: all 316 tests across kona-node-service, kona-node, and lokahi pass with all features and zero skips. Full workspace Rust lint passes, including formatting, Clippy, nightly documentation, and upstream-mirror checks. Independent Rust and startup/API reviews have no outstanding findings. Full devnet acceptance tests were not rerun locally.

topPRs.title: op-deployer,op-chain-ops!: run every deploy script on forge and delete the Go script host
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
This PR is split into a stack for review: #23663 → #23664 → #23665 → #23666 → #23667 → #23668 → #23669. The stack has later review fixes; this PR stays open as the CI-green reference.

op-deployer ran its deploy scripts on `op-chain-ops/script`, an in-process Go EVM. That host needs EVM hooks that only op-geth has (cheatcode precompiles, pranks, no code-size limit), so it blocks the move to upstream go-ethereum (#20266). After this PR, forge is the only script engine, and the Go host and `op-chain-ops/interopgen` are deleted.

**Effect on users**

- op-deployer runs forge for every deployment, and anvil for `prepare` and `continue`. It downloads the pinned Foundry release on Linux and macOS when the tools are not on PATH. The Docker images ship both.
- Genesis deployments (`apply --deployment-target genesis`, op-e2e, sysgo) run the scripts offline on forge. The L1 and L2 genesis output does not change: before the switch, a differential test found equal state roots from both engines on eight reference intents.
- Live `apply` and `bootstrap` broadcast with forge, one transaction at a time, and no longer through op-service's txmgr. As txmgr did, each transaction gets the node's gas estimate just before forge sends it, a tip of at least 1 gwei, and a fee cap of twice the base fee (at least 1 gwei) plus the tip. Unlike txmgr, forge does not bump the fee of, or resubmit, a stuck transaction. forge gets the deployer key in a temporary encrypted keystore that only the user can read, never on its command line.
- `prepare` and `continue` simulate the deployment on an ephemeral anvil fork of the L1, as the deployer, without its key. `continue` then checks the simulated transactions and replays them to L1 through txmgr.
- op-deployer never compiles. It refuses a contracts bundle that would make forge compile, or whose scripts have no `runWithBytes` entrypoint, and it stops forge as soon as forge starts to compile. So a bundle must come from the contracts release of the same op-deployer release: an `https://` or `file://` bundle of an earlier release is refused (`tag://` locators were already rejected). The default, `embedded`, works.
- A contracts bundle is a forge project, so op-deployer does not trust its `foundry.toml`: scripts run without the FFI cheatcode, with file access only to the artifacts and to op-deployer's state directory, and forge scripts and anvil inherit only the environment variables that they need (`verify-contract` keeps the full environment, for its API key). anvil listens on loopback without CORS.
- forge runs need the `lib/` sources of the bundle but no solc compiler. Each forge script loads every artifact of the project, about 1.3 GB, so forge runs take one of `GOMAXPROCS/2` slots per host.
- forge's output goes to stderr. A failed script reports its revert reason.
- Removed: the `calldata` and `noop` deployment targets, `op-deployer manage`, the `--use-forge` and `--forge-slow-broadcast` flags, the Windows release binaries and `DeploymentCalldata` in `state.json`. contracts-bedrock loses the `InteropMigration` script and `DummyCaller`.

**Reasons the diff does not show**

- Every forge run uses its own copy of the compile cache and its own broadcast directory, so that concurrent runs (devstack) do not interfere.
- Each broadcast sends one transaction at a time. Without `--slow`, forge waited forever when a node dropped one of several transactions that it sent at once.
- Bundle builds run one `forge script` to warm the script cache, as CI's `forge-build` already does. A single script's compile can choose other solc versions than the project build, and then forge compiles on the first run. The builds then check that a second run compiles nothing, and fail if it does.
- The interop harness and sysgo now run the interop migration on a live L1 through an EIP-7702 delegation from the ProxyAdmin owner, not in the genesis state. The L1 activates Prague at genesis for this.
- The test `RetryProxy` (op-service) now gives a client error (4xx, but not 429) to the client at once. forge calls methods such as `anvil_nodeInfo` that a proxyd endpoint answers with 403, and the proxy held each of these calls for about 40 s of retries, so the Sepolia tests of `init` timed out.
- sysgo waits for the L1 transaction index before it deploys: geth rejects receipt queries until its first indexing pass is done, and forge stops after a few quick retries.
- #23309 (genesis-output changes) is not in this PR, on purpose. It changes genesis output, which this PR must not do.
- CI jobs that run op-deployer from the checkout (op-e2e, sysgo, kona proof tests) now check out the contracts `lib/` submodules: forge reads the sources to check its compile cache, where the Go host read only artifact JSON.
- forge runs are not `--offline`: offline, forge requires every solc version of the cache installed even when it compiles nothing. Online, it resolves them from its built-in list and runs the cached artifacts.
- The `forge` package tests (anvil fork, compile stop, sandbox, environment, slots) run in CI only after #23643, which removes the package from the CI exclusion list.

**Review findings not fixed here**

- Live `apply`/`bootstrap` could keep txmgr by simulating on an anvil fork and replaying, as `continue` does. The #23300 plan chose `forge script --broadcast` for live deploys; this is a follow-up if fee bumping matters for these one-time deployments.
- The op-e2e interop harness and sysgo could share one `opcm.MigrateInput` type, and sysgo could check that its rollup configs and dependency set name the same chains, as interopgen did. Both are follow-ups.
- `opcm.NewForgeClient` takes no context for the forge download, and `opcm.PermissionedGameStartingAnchorRoot` now has only test users. Both are unchanged.
- Security review, not fixed: `continue` checks the sender, target, type and value of the call it replays, but not its calldata against the prepared input (that needs the script's encoding in Go); the RPC URL stays on the command line of forge and anvil, which have no environment binding for it; a crash during a broadcast can leave the encrypted keystore and its password file in a directory that only the user can read (forge refuses a password pipe); and a forge binary in the cache directory is trusted by its version.

Closes #23300, #23301, #23302, #23304, #23305, #23306, #23307 and #23308.

BREAKING CHANGE: The Go packages `op-chain-ops/script`, `op-chain-ops/interopgen`, `op-deployer/pkg/env`, `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/manage` and `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/upgrade` are removed. So are `opcm.Scripts`, the script-host `opcm` constructors, the `opcm.*ViaForge` functions (now `opcm.DeploySuperchain`, `opcm.DeployImplementations`, `opcm.DeployOPChain`, `opcm.DeployAltDA`, `opcm.DeployDisputeGame`, `opcm.DeployMIPS`, `opcm.DeployAlphabetVM`, `opcm.ReadImplementationAddresses` and `opcm.ReadSuperchainDeployment`, which take an `opcm.ForgeEnv`), `ApplyPipelineOpts.PrivateKey`, `UseForge` and `ReceiptQueryInterval`, and in `broadcaster` the `Broadcaster` interface, `CalldataBroadcaster`, `CaptureBroadcaster`, `NoopBroadcaster` and `BroadcastCreate2`. Go programs run Solidity scripts with forge, for example through op-deployer's `forge` package, take the upgrade input types from `opcm`, and build interop test worlds with an op-deployer intent. op-deployer users get forge and anvil from the release images, or let op-deployer download them. Users of `--use-forge`, `--forge-slow-broadcast`, or the `calldata` and `noop` targets drop them; forge is always used. Intents that point at an `https://` or `file://` bundle of an earlier contracts release use `embedded` instead. To move chains to interop, call `OPContractsManagerV2.migrate` as a delegatecall from the chains' ProxyAdmin owner, for example from a superchain-ops task.

completedItems.title: ci: enforce shfmt formatting on shell scripts
